From 6f02c6b196036dbb6defb4647d8707d29b7fe95b Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Tom Ryan <ryan36005@gmail.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 22:20:02 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] io_uring: fix physical SQE bounds check for SQE_MIXED
 128-byte ops

When IORING_SETUP_SQE_MIXED is used without IORING_SETUP_NO_SQARRAY,
the boundary check for 128-byte SQE operations in io_init_req()
validated the logical SQ head position rather than the physical SQE
index.

The existing check:

  !(ctx->cached_sq_head & (ctx->sq_entries - 1))

ensures the logical position isn't at the end of the ring, which is
correct for NO_SQARRAY rings where physical == logical. However, when
sq_array is present, an unprivileged user can remap any logical
position to an arbitrary physical index via sq_array. Setting
sq_array[N] = sq_entries - 1 places a 128-byte operation at the last
physical SQE slot, causing the 128-byte memcpy in
io_uring_cmd_sqe_copy() to read 64 bytes past the end of the SQE
array.

Replace the cached_sq_head alignment check with a direct validation
of the physical SQE index, which correctly handles both sq_array and
NO_SQARRAY cases.

Fixes: 1cba30bf9fdd ("io_uring: add support for IORING_SETUP_SQE_MIXED")
Signed-off-by: Tom Ryan <ryan36005@gmail.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260310052003.72871-1-ryan36005@gmail.com
Signed-off-by: Jens Axboe <axboe@kernel.dk>

diff --git a/io_uring/io_uring.c b/io_uring/io_uring.c
index 20fdc442e014..20ec8fdafcae 100644
--- a/io_uring/io_uring.c
+++ b/io_uring/io_uring.c
@@ -1745,7 +1745,7 @@ static int io_init_req(struct io_ring_ctx *ctx, struct io_kiocb *req,
 		 * well as 2 contiguous entries.
 		 */
 		if (!(ctx->flags & IORING_SETUP_SQE_MIXED) || *left < 2 ||
-		    !(ctx->cached_sq_head & (ctx->sq_entries - 1)))
+		    (unsigned)(sqe - ctx->sq_sqes) >= ctx->sq_entries - 1)
 			return io_init_fail_req(req, -EINVAL);

-- 
2.34.1

### Summary of Modifications

#### Modifications in each file

**`io_uring/io_uring.c` (single change)**

- **Old line (line 1748):**  
  `!(ctx->cached_sq_head & (ctx->sq_entries - 1))`  
  This checked that the logical SQ head (`cached_sq_head`) is not at the end of the ring (alignment with `sq_entries - 1`). This was correct only when physical SQE indices equal logical indices (i.e., when `IORING_SETUP_NO_SQARRAY` is set).

- **New line:**  
  `(unsigned)(sqe - ctx->sq_sqes) >= ctx->sq_entries - 1`  
  This directly checks that the **physical** SQE index (computed by subtracting the base `sq_sqes` pointer from the `sqe` pointer) is not the last entry in the physical SQE array. This works correctly regardless of whether `sq_array` is used to remap logical positions to arbitrary physical indices.

#### Relationships between modifications

The change is a single, self-contained fix in the `io_init_req()` function. It corrects a security/reliability bug where an unprivileged user could exploit a 128-byte (two-entry) SQE operation combined with the `IORING_SETUP_SQE_MIXED` flag and a custom `sq_array` mapping to cause an out-of-bounds read (64 bytes past the end of the SQE array). The old condition only checked the logical head position, failing to account for arbitrary physical remapping via `sq_array`. The new condition uses the absolute physical SQE index, ensuring the 128-byte operation’s second entry physically exists within the SQE array. This maintains the intended restriction that a 128-byte operation cannot be placed at the very last SQE slot (since it needs two contiguous physical slots).

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
if (!(ctx->flags & IORING_SETUP_SQE_MIXED) || *left < 2 ||
    !(ctx->cached_sq_head & (ctx->sq_entries - 1)))
Reason:
The bounds check uses the logical SQ head position (`ctx->cached_sq_head`) instead of the physical SQE index. When `sq_array` is present, an unprivileged user can remap any logical index to an arbitrary physical index via `sq_array`. By setting `sq_array[N] = ctx->sq_entries - 1`, a 128-byte operation can be placed at the last physical SQE slot, bypassing the alignment check. This leads to a 64‑byte out‑of‑bounds read in `io_uring_cmd_sqe_copy()`.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
if (!(ctx->flags & IORING_SETUP_SQE_MIXED) || *left < 2 ||
    (unsigned)(sqe - ctx->sq_sqes) >= ctx->sq_entries - 1)
Reason:
The fix replaces the logical head alignment check with a direct validation of the physical SQE index. `sqe - ctx->sq_sqes` gives the physical index of the current SQE. If it is greater than or equal to `ctx->sq_entries - 1`, the operation is at the boundary and cannot be a 128‑byte SQE. This check correctly handles both `sq_array` and `NO_SQARRAY` cases, preventing the out‑of‑bounds read.
